a09f78d50fd042a404dbd277@montreal-poetry.title: Accent Poetry Series: Garth Martens, Loch Baillie, David Gosselin, plus open mic!
a09f78d50fd042a404dbd277@montreal-poetry.description:
Join poets Loch Baillie, David Gosselin, and Garth Martens at Bar Le Record for an evening of poetry at the Accent Poetry Series, a Montreal-based literary series and open mic. The open mic follows the featured readings.

Montréal, Québec — Accent Poetry Series Sunday, Oct. 18, 8:00–11:00 p.m. Bar Le Record 7622 rue Saint-Hubert, Montréal, QC H2R 2N6

LOCH BAILLIE

In his highly anticipated, breathtakingly intimate debut, Loch Baillie pens an unfiltered queer Bildungsroman that traces both a geographical and emotional journey from his birthplace in New England to where he comes to settle in Quebec.

Raw and confessional, River Running dives gracefully into the intangible concept of home, be it person or place. “No more metaphors tonight,” writes Baillie, “I come to tell you nothing / but the truth.” This collection probes at memory and love, identity and grief, with achingly gentle hands, sifting through the fragments one both leaves behind and becomes.

Loch Baillie is a writer, editor, and teacher based in Québec. He is the author of two poetry chapbooks, ice, dove, parachute (Cactus Press) and Citronella (Anstruther Press), as well as the full-length collection River Running (Goose Lane Editions). His next book, Head Split in Half, doubles as his Master’s thesis at Université Laval. Loch currently serves as associate poetry editor at Plenitude Magazine and as a board director for the Quebec Writers’ Federation. Find him everywhere @lochbaillie.

DAVID B. GOSSELIN

David Gosselin is a writer, researcher, translator and filmmaker. He is the founder of the multimedia platform Age of Muses on Substack, where he produces adaptations of both modern and classic works of poetry and literature, along with films, stories and dialogues. He also runs New Lyre Magazine, the print organ.

GARTH MARTENS

In his first collection since the Governor General’s–nominated Prologue for the Age of Consequence, Garth Martens adds an autobiographical lens to his concerns about class and labour.

A mother disappears. A son struggles to make sense of the life she left behind. Set against the stark northern Alberta of the 1980s and 90s, Who Else in the Dark Headed There follows a man reaching through time to find the child he was and the father he is becoming. Beneath this waking world is another world, of the overheard, of the unsaid. To enter is to find a lyricism finely wrought and hallucinatory, a depth of feeling and fidelity to metaphor in all its guises—but most of all an urgent relationship with language. Here, in a reconstruction of childhood’s rooms, Garth Martens approaches the past not as a record but as a pressure, a “muscled concentration” that reorders, resuscitates, and redoubts.

Poems of intense emotion, the torque on the language extreme—as it must be, reaching this far into the dark, this honestly. —Jan Zwicky

This is hard stuff, looked at with a cold eye. It’s beautiful, fierce, profoundly defensive, smart as heck, and intrusive. —Harold Rhenisch, The BC Review

Arresting fragments emerge from a relentless invocation of half scenes, stitched together with the singular logic of poetic memory (which is to say, with mystery.) —Literary Review of Canada

The fragmented poems showcase an urgent relationship with language that is sensory, emotive and captivating. —CBC Books

Garth Martens is the author of Who Else in the Dark Headed There (Biblioasis, 2026), the chapbook Remediation (JackPine, 2018), and Prologue for the Age of Consequence (Anansi, 2014), for which he was a finalist for the Governor General’s Literary Award in Poetry. He is also a past winner of the Bronwen Wallace Award for Emerging Writers. His poetry appears in Dark Mountain Project, BODY Literature, Poetry Ireland, Hazlitt, This Magazine, Fiddlehead, Vallum, Grain, Prism, Grain, and Best Canadian Poetry. He is co-founder of Palabra Flamenco, a literary flamenco ensemble that joins traditional flamenco dance and music with poetry and oral storytelling. He lives on Vancouver Island. Find him on Instagram @garthmartens.

ACCENT POETRY SERIES

Established in 2019 by Devon Gallant and Luc-Antoine Chiasson, the Accent Reading Series was founded out of a desire to provide Montreal authors with a reliable venue to congregate and share their work with one another. Infamous for our unlimited open mic spots and the dreaded five-minute bell, over thirty open mic readers have graced the Accent stage on any given night.

0a0a6046973dc43fdd8a496f@montreal-poetry.title: Rencontre avec Martine Delvaux
0a0a6046973dc43fdd8a496f@montreal-poetry.venue: Librairie Résonance Bookstore, 40 Beaubien East, Montréal
0a0a6046973dc43fdd8a496f@montreal-poetry.description:
La librairie Résonance a le plaisir d'accueillir Martine Delvaux afin de discuter de son plus récent ouvrage, Divas. 
Vous êtes invité.es à venir assister à une discussion entre Delvaux et moi, suivra ensuite une période de question.
Gratuit
Voix incontournable du féminisme au Canada, Martine Delvaux livre une enquête sensible et ample sur la voix de celles qu’on a si souvent tenté de réduire au silence.
« Il ne s’agit pas ici d’attraper les divas, toutes les divas, dans le but de les collectionner, d’en faire une encyclopédie ou un dictionnaire, de coller sur elles des connaissances exhaustives, un savoir universitaire, il ne s’agit pas de les épingler comme on le fait avec les papillons. Non, il s’agit simplement d’en choisir certaines, d’écouter leurs voix monter pour y puiser une leçon de création et d’ambition, en même temps que d’humanité et d’humilité. » Martine Delvaux, extrait Divas

68f6ff4429627a81b03de4cd@montreal-poetry.title: SESSION REWIND - DJ POIRIER IL N'Y A PAS DE SUD...
68f6ff4429627a81b03de4cd@montreal-poetry.venue: Librairie Résonance Bookstore, 40 Beaubien East, Montréal
68f6ff4429627a81b03de4cd@montreal-poetry.description:
Nous sommes ravis d'accueillir une figure marquante de la musique électronique au Québec lors du 25ème anniversaire de la sortie de son album Il n'y a que le sud...
Figure incontournable de Montréal, Poirier s’est imposé par une approche créative et éclectique de la production électronique. Des atmosphères lo-fi scintillantes de ses débuts aux rythmes entraînants inspirés du soca dans ses projets plus récents, sa signature musicale puise dans une vaste diversité de traditions sonores, affirmant sa place sur la scène internationale.
Avec plus de 25 ans de parcours, le DJ, producteur et auteur-compositeur a construit une discographie importante sur des labels tels que Ninja Tune et Wonderwheel Recordings. Il a également signé plus de 55 remix officiels, son approche recherchée ayant été sollicitée par des artistes comme Gotan Project, Gilles Peterson, Guts, Salif Keita, Nickodemus, João Selva, Flavia Coelho, Popcaan ou Busy Signal, entre autres.
Déroulement de la soirée: 
19h Introduction de l'artiste19h05 Écoute de l'album20h Discussion avec l'artiste
Le vinyle Il n'y a pas de sud ainsi que son plus récent ouvrage Flip the Script Sounds Good seront vendus sur place.
